not_yet.text: The stair goes on up from the landing's far side, turning left out of sight. At the top of the turn, a door: you can't see it, but you can feel the singing coming through it, the way you feel a cart go by through a floor.
A great many voices, close now. All at the one thing, and none of them getting to the end of it.
The ember leans to the stair. Not much. The way the beacon cradles leaned to it, every island, and past whatever you held out over them.
The lantern room. The chapter hasn't chosen yet. The hand, the Provost said. Not the choosing.
You find you've stepped back. Not yet. Your feet are very sure about it, and this time you know why.

chosen.text: The stair goes on up from the landing's far side, turning left out of sight, into the singing.
The ember leans to it. The chapter has sat, and written down that it does not choose. Your feet don't stop you this time.

up.text: Eight. There's no notch for it on any taper. The stair turns once more and stops at a door: oak, three iron bands, the twin of the one at the foot. The singing is on the other side of it, close enough that the wood hums under your hand.

again.text: The stair on up to the lantern room. The door's as you left it, and the singing comes down past it.

choice.text: Go back up to the lantern room.
